title: Component-level `visibleWhen` binds no `record` on record pages — every `record.*` predicate fails soft to permanently visible, on every block
body:
Filed unassigned by the dev agent working #5401 (session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`), as the census that card asked for as its first deliverable. Priority and lane routing belong to this repo's PM seat — filing with the measurements, not a grade.

**Related: #5401** — that card's re-ruling depends on this one. It is not a duplicate: #5401 is scoped to `record:alert`; this is the platform-wide hole the census turned up underneath it.

## The defect

`@objectstack/spec` documents the component node's `visibleWhen` as *"Visibility predicate (CEL) — component rendered only when TRUE. Binds `record`, `current_user`, `page.*`"* (`packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts:189`).

**`record` is bound nowhere on that path.** `SchemaRenderer` builds the evaluator that decides `visibleWhen` from exactly three sources (`packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx:371-380`, `:419-424`):

- the ambient predicate scope from app-shell's `ExpressionProvider` — `current_user`, `user`, `ctx.user`, `os.user`, `app`, `data`, `features`;
- `data: dataSource`, which is the data-source **connector adapter** from `SchemaRendererContext`, not the row;
- `page: pageVariables`.

`ExpressionProvider` is mounted with `data={{}}` at both of its call sites (`console/AppContent.tsx:877`, `views/RecordFormPage.tsx:270`), and `RecordDetailView` renders the page through `SchemaRenderer` with no `data` prop, so the region components get `NO_DATA_SOURCE`. The record lives in `RecordContext`, which this evaluator never reads.

Because the surface is fail-soft, an unresolvable predicate resolves to **shown**. So a `record.*` gate does not merely misfire — it renders the component unconditionally, which is a visibility gate that silently does not gate.

## Measured, not reasoned

Through the shipped pipeline (`PredicateScopeProvider` carrying the scope `ExpressionProvider` really mounts, plus `RecordContextProvider`), on `objectui` `c40f3b8ca`. Harness committed at `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/__tests__/record-alert.visibleWhen.evidence.test.tsx` on branch `claude/issue-5401-record-alert-visiblewhen` (no PR — see #5401):

| node-level `visibleWhen` | record | `record:alert` | `record:path` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `false` (constant) | any | HIDDEN | HIDDEN |
| `current_user.email_verified == false` | any | HIDDEN | — |
| `current_user.email_verified == true` | any | SHOWN | — |
| `record.status == 'in_review'` | `status: 'done'` | **SHOWN** | — |
| `record.status == 'in_review'` | `status: 'in_review'` | **SHOWN** | — |
| `record.status == 'done'` | `status: 'done'` | — | **SHOWN** |
| `record.status == 'zzz'` | `status: 'done'` | — | **SHOWN** |
| absent | any | SHOWN | SHOWN |

Every bold row is the defect: the two polarities of the same predicate produce the same verdict, so the gate is inert.

**Counter-probes for each zero.** The constant-`false` and `current_user` rows are the paired controls — the same blocks CAN be hidden through this channel, so "SHOWN" above is a verdict rather than an inability to render or an inability to hide. The `absent` row pairs against every HIDDEN cell, so "hidden" is not "never rendered".

## Why it is easy to miss

Constants and `current_user` predicates work, and those are what a smoke test reaches for. `#5401`'s browser run used `visibleWhen: {cel, 'false'}` and concluded the mechanism was alive and honoured generally — true for that predicate, and only that class of predicate.

The one component that gets `record` right does it in its **props**, not on the node: `record:alert` evaluates `properties.visible` through `toPredicateInput` + `useCondition`, which merges `usePredicateRecordContext(record)` over the ambient scope. Measured, that gate keeps its verdict on both polarities. `@objectstack/spec` already knows this — `RecordAlertProps` declares `visible` and aliases `visibleWhen` onto it, and `component.zod.ts` carves this component out of the "move visibility up to the node" guidance for exactly this reason.

## Second, smaller defect on the same chain — precedence

`SchemaRenderer` hoists `properties.*` onto the node, then tests `visible` **before** `visibleWhen` (`SchemaRenderer.tsx:511` vs `:519`). A node declaring both therefore has its `visibleWhen` silently ignored. Measured identically on `record:alert`, `record:path`, `page:card` and `element:text`, so it is generic to the chain. This is the mechanism behind the browser symptom #5401 reported.

## Not proposing a fix here

Which way this should go is a real decision, not a mechanical repair — binding `record` into the node evaluator would give `visibleWhen` a scope it has never had and would change the verdict of any shipped `record.*` node predicate from "shown" to whatever it actually evaluates to. That wants a ruling, and it is entangled with #5401's. Reporting the census; leaving the call to the maintainer.
